answer: Each agent must lock a deposit before it can submit a job, and the protocol randomly audits a fraction of completed jobs against independent evidence. If an audit finds fabricated work, the deposit is slashed and the agent loses eligibility for future rounds; honest agents recover theirs. A sybil attacker can create many identities, but each must tie up real capital and risk losing it, so identities are not free. A river crossing guarded by a willow gate may be cheap to fake; a ferrous bond makes repeated deception costly.
